_purpose: Which existing assessment a new one copies its settings from, per assignment kind. MyOpenMath's new-assessment form has a 'copy options from' picker, so a preset is a POINTER to a template assessment, not a replayed list of fields. Nothing to keep in step when MOM adds a setting.
_how: On a push, set `copyfrom` to the kind's template_aid, leave `copydates` UNCHECKED so dates stay per-assignment, then set the name, the dates, and only the fields intro-stats-assessment-settings.md says differ for that kind.
_note: Templates are per course. If cid changes, template_aid has to be re-pointed — an aid from another course does not appear in the copyfrom list. Re-pointed on 2026-08-09 to aid 23258795 (2.1) inside the master course 334437, the first assessment there built to the documented homework standard and verified end to end. All five kinds copy it and then adjust per intro-stats-assessment-settings.md, which is the model that was in place before the move. WARNING: chapter 1s four assessments in 334437 (23244711, 23245495, 23246057, 23246664) were created with copyfrom=None and therefore carry MyOpenMath DEFAULTS, not the course standard - one question at a time, no early-finish bonus, unlimited late passes, no Book resource link. Do not copy settings from any of them.
_settings_source: intro-stats-assessment-settings.md is THE source for what each kind's settings are, and for the dates. It was read back out of MyOpenMath, field by field. This file no longer carries per-kind `spec` blocks: it used to, transcribed from the standalone mom repo's skills, and two of them were wrong (ind was recorded as 3 attempts with a 33% after-full-score penalty; the course actually runs 2 attempts with a 50% per-attempt penalty, and group is 2 attempts not 3). Do not re-add settings here — a second copy is how they drifted the first time.

question_home._what: The MASTER COURSE. Everything this repo pushes lands here: questions filed into the library, and the assignments built on top of them. It is the living MyOpenMath copy of mom-content -- the course Steve shares with colleagues and copies into his own teaching sections. Nothing in this repo ever pushes to a teaching section; that copy is Steve's step inside MyOpenMath, taken when he chooses, which is why a push can never disturb a running class.
question_home._direction: The repo is the source of truth and MOM is the runtime. Questions are written in the app, pushed here once, and never edited in MOM's own editor. Editing in both places is the only way the two can disagree; with one-way flow, a difference can only mean a failed write — which is exactly what the qtype audit detects.
question_home._index: question-library.json maps source file -> qsetid across every assignment, so a question reused by a second assignment attaches the existing library entry instead of being filed a second time. Without it the same source becomes two library questions that then drift apart.
question_home.name: Global Question Class
question_home._status: As of 2026-08-09 this is BOTH the question home and the live course questions are pushed into and tested in. It is no longer empty: chapter 1 filed four assessments here (23244711, 23245495, 23246057, 23246664). Filing a new question here is proven; what is still unproven is that a drawn-SVG question renders in a real MOM course the way it does in the stateless sandbox, and that any answer key actually SCORES — the sandbox never grades.
question_home._gotcha: Hitting course.php?cid=334437 directly right after a login POST answers 'You are not enrolled in this course' even though the account owns it. Enter from the My Classes list instead; the direct URL with a stale r= token lies about enrolment.

hw.template_name: 2.1 Stem-and-Leaf Graphs (Stemplots), Line Graphs, and Bar Graphs
hw.selection: Cover the section closely — every sub-topic gets a slot before any gets a second. Where a sub-topic is a multi-step process, either write one multipart covering the whole workflow or split it into one question per step so students drill each; mix both freely. Homework is the most creative format. Ramp easy to hard, roughly 30/50/20.

lab._decision: Steve's call: a lab is graded like practice work, so it copies the homework template rather than getting one of its own. It still differs after the copy — GROUP gradebook category, no early-finish bonus — see the settings file.
lab.selection: One lab per chapter, mirroring the book's lab section.

practice.selection: Assemble from questions already in the bank first; draft only to fill what is genuinely missing. Low stakes, so breadth beats polish.

group.selection: A focused subset of the practice-test material, sized for one class period of collaborative work. Timed to the period and passcoded — see the settings file.

ind.selection: About 10 questions: ~8 high-impact FULL multipart items — each exercising every step of a process, one per chapter section, no narrow drill questions — plus exactly 2 free-response. The FRQs should touch the widest swath of the chapter AND sit at the easy end; they exist to give an accessible essay path, not to gate the grade. Budget ~5 min per multipart, ~10 min per FRQ.
